study_material.title: Permutations and Combinations - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Permutations count arrangements (order matters); combinations count selections (order does not). Decide which one the question needs, then apply the factorial formulas. Repeated letters, together/never-together constraints and circular tables are the standard twists.

concepts.heading: 1. Multiplication Principle
concepts.body: If a task has k independent stages with n1, n2, ... choices, total ways = n1 x n2 x ... . Three shirts and four trousers give 12 outfits. This principle underlies every formula in the chapter.

concepts.heading: 2. Permutations
concepts.body: nPr = n!/(n-r)! counts ordered arrangements of r items from n distinct items. All n items: n! ways. Words with repeated letters: divide by the factorial of each repeat count - APPLE has 5!/2! = 60 arrangements.

concepts.heading: 3. Combinations
concepts.body: nCr = n!/(r!(n-r)!) counts unordered selections. nCr = nC(n-r) - choosing r to keep equals choosing n-r to discard. Handshakes among n people = nC2 = n(n-1)/2.

concepts.heading: 4. Together and Apart
concepts.body: To keep a group together, glue it into one block: arrange the blocks, then arrange within the block. 4 boys and 3 girls with girls together: treat girls as 1 unit - 5! x 3! = 720. 'Never together' = total - together.

concepts.heading: 5. Circular Arrangements
concepts.body: n distinct people around a round table: (n-1)! arrangements (rotations are identical). If clockwise and anticlockwise are considered the same (a necklace), divide by 2: (n-1)!/2.

shortcut_methods: Ask 'does order matter?' before anything else
nCr = nC(n-r) - compute the smaller side
Constraint problems: handle the constraint first, count the rest after
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide by repeated-letter factorials
Using n! instead of (n-1)! for circular tables
study_material.summary: Order matters: permutation. Order doesn't: combination. Repeats divide, blocks glue, circles lose one factorial.
quick_revision_notes: Together = block trick; never = total - together

solved_examples.question: In how many ways can 5 different books be arranged on a shelf?
In how many ways can the letters of APPLE be arranged?
How many handshakes occur among 10 people if each shakes hands with every other exactly once?
4 boys and 3 girls must sit in a row with all girls together. How many arrangements?
solved_examples.step_by_step: Glue girls: 5 units in 5! = 120 ways; girls among themselves 3! = 6. Total 720.
